# Green Goods in Human Terms

Use these cards when explaining Green Goods to a teammate, community, partner, or agent. Meaning and maturity are shown separately so a well-defined or deployed concept is never mistaken for an available product flow.

## Garden

**In plain language:** A community and its shared place

**Why it matters:** It gives people, roles, records, and funds one accountable home.

**Who touches it:** Gardener · Operator · Evaluator · Funder · Community Member

**Example:** A neighborhood garden coordinating planting, evidence, and funding.

**Relationships:** has-many vault · has-tree hat

**Also called:** community garden

**Do not confuse with:** a personal wallet · a single project

**Current maturity:** available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration integrated.

**Evidence:** `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json` — Arbitrum deployment includes the Garden token, account, and module.<br />`packages/client/src/views/Public/GardenDetail.tsx` — The client exposes a public Garden surface. (verified 2026-08-15)

**Public-safe wording:** Communities can organize people and records around a shared Garden.

## Action

**In plain language:** A reusable work instruction

**Why it matters:** It makes expected work and evidence clear before anyone submits it.

**Who touches it:** Operator · Gardener

**Example:** Plant native species and capture before-and-after photos.

**Relationships:** enabled-by-domain-mask garden

**Also called:** work template

**Do not confuse with:** Work · Commitment

**Current maturity:** available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration integrated.

**Evidence:** `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json` — Arbitrum deployment includes the Action registry.<br />`packages/client/src/views/Public/Actions.tsx` — The client exposes public Action records. (verified 2026-08-15)

## Work

**In plain language:** A field record of completed activity

**Why it matters:** It turns local action into portable evidence without waiting for approval to exist.

**Who touches it:** Gardener · Operator

**Example:** A photo and description submitted as a Work attestation, then approved separately.

**Relationships:** instance-of action · performed-in garden

**Also called:** work submission · field record

**Do not confuse with:** Work Approval · Assessment

**Current maturity:** available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration integrated.

**Evidence:** `packages/contracts/src/resolvers/Work.sol` — Work submission creates its EAS attestation before review.<br />`packages/client/src/views/Home/Garden/Work.tsx` — Gardeners have a product surface for Work. (verified 2026-08-15)

**Public-safe wording:** Gardeners can document Work in the field and sync it when connectivity returns. Operators review Work and record an approval or rejection separately. Green Goods is building the activation path that turns approved Work into portable Impact Certificates.

## Assessment

**In plain language:** A baseline and strategy

**Why it matters:** It states what a place needs and what good evidence should demonstrate.

**Who touches it:** Evaluator · Operator

**Example:** A soil-health baseline with targets and selected Actions.

**Relationships:** frames garden

**Also called:** baseline

**Do not confuse with:** Work Approval

**Current maturity:** available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration integrated.

**Evidence:** `packages/contracts/src/resolvers/Assessment.sol` — Assessment resolver accepts Evaluator or Operator attestations.<br />`packages/client/src/views/Home/Garden/Assessment.tsx` — The client exposes the Garden Assessment flow. (verified 2026-08-15)

**Public-safe wording:** Assessments make the baseline, plan, and evidence standard explicit.

## Hypercert

**In plain language:** A portable impact certificate

**Why it matters:** It lets approved contribution records become a fundable impact claim.

**Who touches it:** Funder · Gardener · Operator

**Example:** A certificate bundling a season of approved Work.

**Relationships:** bundles work · minted-for garden

**Also called:** Impact Certificate

**Do not confuse with:** Attestation · Work Approval

**Current maturity:** in-build — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation inactive; integration partial.

**Evidence:** `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json` — Hypercert module and minting contracts are deployed; product activation remains deployment/indexing dependent. (verified 2026-08-15)

**Public-safe wording:** Green Goods is building the activation path that turns approved Work into portable Impact Certificates.

## Vault

**In plain language:** A Garden's long-term treasury

**Why it matters:** Principal can remain deposited while yield supports ongoing work.

**Who touches it:** Funder · Operator

**Example:** A funder endows a Garden and the yield supports operations.

**Relationships:** treasury-of garden

**Also called:** endowment

**Do not confuse with:** Cookie Jar

**Current maturity:** available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration integrated.

**Evidence:** `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json` — Octant factory and module are present in the Arbitrum deployment.<br />`packages/client/src/views/Public/Vaults.tsx` — The public client exposes active Vault flows. (verified 2026-08-15)

**Public-safe wording:** Support can meet near-term needs or remain deposited so yield supports work over time.

## Cookie Jar

**In plain language:** A bounded near-term fund

**Why it matters:** It supports smaller operational needs with explicit claim limits.

**Who touches it:** Operator · Gardener · Funder

**Example:** An allowlisted member claims a capped amount for supplies.

**Relationships:** discretionary-fund-of garden

**Also called:** jar

**Do not confuse with:** Vault

**Current maturity:** available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration integrated.

**Evidence:** `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json` — Cookie Jar factory and module are present in the Arbitrum deployment.<br />`packages/client/src/views/Public/Cookies.tsx` — The public client exposes active Cookie Jar records. (verified 2026-08-15)

**Public-safe wording:** Support can meet near-term needs or remain deposited so yield supports work over time.

## Attestation

**In plain language:** A signed public record

**Why it matters:** It makes a claim portable and independently readable.

**Who touches it:** Gardener · Operator · Evaluator · Community Member

**Example:** A Work submission and its later approval are two attestations.

**Relationships:** records work · records assessment

**Also called:** EAS record

**Do not confuse with:** Hypercert

**Current maturity:** available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration integrated.

**Evidence:** `packages/contracts/config/schemas.json` — Registered Green Goods EAS schema definitions. (verified 2026-08-15)

## Hat

**In plain language:** A portable role and permission

**Why it matters:** It makes garden authority explicit and revocable.

**Who touches it:** Operator · Gardener · Evaluator · Funder · Community Member

**Example:** An Operator Hat allows its wearer to approve Work.

**Relationships:** authority-in garden

**Also called:** role Hat

**Do not confuse with:** persona

**Current maturity:** available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration integrated.

**Evidence:** `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json` — Hats module is present in the Arbitrum deployment.<br />`packages/client/src/components/Public/PublicWhoTendsAGarden.tsx` — The public client explains active Garden roles. (verified 2026-08-15)

**Public-safe wording:** Communities can organize people and records around a shared Garden.

## Season

**In plain language:** A shared period of coordinated work

**Why it matters:** It gives planning and reflection a calm common rhythm.

**Who touches it:** Gardener · Operator · Evaluator

**Example:** A quarter of Actions, Work, and Assessments.

**Relationships:** formalized-by commitment-cycle

**Also called:** garden season

**Do not confuse with:** Commitment Cycle

**Current maturity:** planned — implementation partial; deployment not-applicable; activation not-applicable; integration partial.

**Evidence:** `.plans/active/commitment-pooling/contract-spec.md` — Commitment Cycle type Season is implemented onchain, but the product season surface is not available. (verified 2026-08-15)

## Need

**In plain language:** A community need and desired outcome

**Why it matters:** It lets communities name what should change before solutions or funding are proposed.

**Who touches it:** Community Member · Operator · Funder

**Example:** Reliable shade is needed at a neighborhood gathering place.

**Relationships:** raised-in garden · addressed-by commitment · recorded-as attestation

**Also called:** community need

**Do not confuse with:** Commitment · Action

**Current maturity:** planned — implementation not-implemented; deployment not-deployed; activation inactive; integration not-integrated.

**Evidence:** `.plans/active/community-interface/status.json` — Community Needs contract, state/API, and UI lanes remain blocked. (verified 2026-08-15)

**Public-safe wording:** Community Needs is a planned layer, not a feature people can use today.

## Commitment Pool

**In plain language:** A governed home for promises

**Why it matters:** It gives a Garden rules and bounds for coordinating offers and requests.

**Who touches it:** Operator · Gardener · Community Member

**Example:** A Garden pool coordinates transport offers under a charter.

**Relationships:** anchored-to garden

**Also called:** pool

**Do not confuse with:** Vault · Cookie Jar

**Current maturity:** deployed-not-available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration not-integrated.

**Evidence:** `.plans/active/commitment-pooling/status.json` — Pooling is unpaused and 18 pools are receipt-verified; indexer/shared/UI lanes remain blocked. (verified 2026-08-15)

**Public-safe wording:** The coordination protocol is deployed, but it is not yet an available Green Goods product flow.

## Commitment Cycle

**In plain language:** A bounded run of a commitment pool

**Why it matters:** It snapshots time and recognition rules for a coherent period.

**Who touches it:** Operator · Gardener

**Example:** A Season cycle opens with a six-role allocation.

**Relationships:** run-of commitment-pool

**Also called:** cycle

**Do not confuse with:** Season

**Current maturity:** deployed-not-available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration not-integrated.

**Evidence:** `packages/contracts/src/interfaces/ICommitmentPoolingModule.sol` — Cycle struct and lifecycle interface are implemented in the deployed pooling boundary. (verified 2026-08-15)

## Commitment Series

**In plain language:** A durable identity for recurring offers

**Why it matters:** It connects repeated Offer instances without merging their histories.

**Who touches it:** Gardener · Operator

**Example:** A weekly transport Offer represented by separate commitments over time.

**Relationships:** scoped-to commitment-pool · groups-offer-instances commitment

**Also called:** series

**Do not confuse with:** Commitment Cycle

**Current maturity:** deployed-not-available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration not-integrated.

**Evidence:** `packages/contracts/src/interfaces/ICommitmentPoolingModule.sol` — Series struct and lifecycle interface are implemented in the deployed pooling boundary. (verified 2026-08-15)

## Commitment

**In plain language:** A bounded promise to offer or request support

**Why it matters:** It makes responsibility, evidence, confirmation, and unit accounting explicit.

**Who touches it:** Gardener · Operator · Community Member

**Example:** Offer three rides, with one lead and two contributors.

**Relationships:** registered-in commitment-pool · optionally-scoped-to commitment-cycle · fulfilled-by work · optionally-instance-of commitment-series · performed-by commitment-contributor · optionally-paid-through commitment-payout-plan

**Also called:** offer · request

**Do not confuse with:** Attestation · Need

**Current maturity:** deployed-not-available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration not-integrated.

**Evidence:** `.plans/active/commitment-pooling/status.json` — Onchain coordination is active; product integration and user surfaces remain blocked. (verified 2026-08-15)

**Public-safe wording:** The coordination protocol is deployed, but it is not yet an available Green Goods product flow. Community Needs is a planned layer, not a feature people can use today.

## Commitment Contributor

**In plain language:** A person credited on a commitment

**Why it matters:** It separates accountable leadership from the people whose verified contribution earns recognition.

**Who touches it:** Gardener · Operator

**Example:** Two gardeners share verified contribution on one fulfilled commitment.

**Relationships:** contributes-to commitment · credited-by work · recognized-in hypercert

**Also called:** contributor

**Do not confuse with:** lead provider · confirmer

**Current maturity:** deployed-not-available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation active; integration not-integrated.

**Evidence:** `packages/contracts/src/interfaces/ICommitmentPoolingModule.sol` — Contributor roster and credit fields are implemented in the deployed pooling boundary. (verified 2026-08-15)

## Commitment Payout Plan

**In plain language:** A frozen split for declared support

**Why it matters:** It proves conservation and contributor amounts before any payment dispatch.

**Who touches it:** Operator · Gardener

**Example:** A Garden retains part and assigns the rest to eligible contributors.

**Relationships:** pays-for commitment · paid-by garden · pays commitment-contributor

**Also called:** payout plan

**Do not confuse with:** recognition weights · payment receipt

**Current maturity:** deployed-not-available — implementation implemented; deployment deployed; activation inactive; integration partial.

**Evidence:** `.plans/active/commitment-pooling/status.json` — Settlement contracts are deployed but paused; value authority and product activation remain disabled. (verified 2026-08-15)

## Gardener

**In plain language:** A person doing and documenting the work

**Why it matters:** Green Goods begins with evidence captured by people caring for a place.

**Who touches it:** Operator · Evaluator

**Example:** A gardener records planting while offline and syncs later.

**Relationships:** —

**Also called:** field contributor

**Do not confuse with:** Commitment Contributor

## Operator

**In plain language:** A person stewarding Garden operations

**Why it matters:** Operators turn community policy into accountable review and coordination.

**Who touches it:** Gardener · Evaluator · Funder · Community Member

**Example:** An operator creates Actions and approves or rejects Work.

**Relationships:** —

**Also called:** Garden Operator · steward

**Do not confuse with:** Evaluator

**Current maturity:** persona, not a product capability.

**Public-safe wording:** Operators review Work and record an approval or rejection separately.

## Evaluator

**In plain language:** A person shaping assessment and impact rigor

**Why it matters:** Evaluators help communities frame baselines, methods, outcomes, and defensible claims.

**Relationships:** —

## Funder

**In plain language:** A person or organization supporting the work

**Why it matters:** Funding connects credible evidence to durable community capacity.
